x2.title: X2 research: agent-skill teaching/explaining ecosystem
x2.imperative: Pocock /teach + /grill-me structure (GitHub if public), explain-diff/change-explaining tools, superpowers/marketplace/IDE 'explain' skills. Transfers vs not for per-user in-flow expert teaching.
x2.finding: Pocock's teach IS public (github.com/mattpocock/skills): MISSION.md (mission-tethering) + NOTES.md (durable prefs) + learning-records/NNNN.md explicitly 'ADR-like' append-only records driving zone-of-proximal-development. grill-me = one-Q Socratic + fact/decision split + shared-understanding gate. STEAL: learning-records-as-ADRs (best fit for expert-but-learning), mission-tethering, docent freshness stamp on any persisted explainer, Copilot's prose+file-bullets output shape. MISMATCH: Pocock's HTML lesson COURSE (novice, out-of-flow); explain-diff tools (Copilot/Cursor) are audience-flat/stateless/no-depth-decision. NULL: all of superpowers teaches the AGENT not the human; the personalized-expert-reader-in-flow niche is UNFILLED (validates 'requires new things').

x3.title: X3 research: education field for teaching a working expert
x3.imperative: ITS architecture, scaffolding/fading + ZPD, expertise-reversal effect + expert blind spot (teaching an expert differs), just-in-time/situated learning + cognitive apprenticeship, concept/prerequisite maps. Beyond X1's classroom-assessment coverage.
x3.finding: DOMINANT FINDING = expertise-reversal effect (Kalyuga/Sweller): for an expert wanting peer register, the whole novice toolkit (worked steps, build-ups, redundant restatement) is ACTIVELY HARMFUL — raises load, reads as condescension. Correct default = minimal/pointer register, add depth ONLY on a detected miss (inverse of novice default). Counter-warning = expert blind spot: agent under-explains the genuinely-NEW delta because it feels obvious. Expertise is concept-LOCAL (expert on A, novice on new B like Matern). ITS 4-component architecture = clean skeleton: concept book = student model (as OVERLAY on a domain map), architecture map = domain model, tutor = tutoring model; drop the instrumented-data pipeline. Fading via contingency rule answers 'when to stop explaining': register DOWN on fluent use, UP on a stumble — a graded dial read off the human's OWN writing. Just-in-time/situated learning validates teach-when-it-comes-up. Concept dependency graph gives depth-gating + ordering (not hard gating).

x4.title: X4 research: how dev tools teach concepts in-flow
x4.imperative: Explanatory compiler errors (Rust --explain), Diataxis explanation quadrant, ADRs/literate programming, IDE/AI 'explain this' features, progressive disclosure/glossary-on-hover. Transfers to K9 explainer + gloss/dial.
x4.finding: Two-tier / short-then-deep is UNIVERSAL (Rust inline vs --explain; tooltip vs full doc; Diataxis reference vs explanation): in-flow default terse, depth PULLED — the concrete shape for K9 + register dial + tutor. Diataxis explanation quadrant ~= spec for K9 (make connections, give the why, discuss alternatives, own perspective, stay bounded) BUT assumes 4 separate docs — interleaving one explanation paragraph into a working stream is UNSOLVED and ours. Compiler-error framing (blocked/erroring reader, corrective tone) is a MISMATCH for a healthy milestone. ADRs = durable context->decision->why-not->consequences teaching unit + immutability/supersession, but written for a future ABSENT reader (mismatch for live single reader). Copilot offloads calibration to the human re-declaring level each time — we must instead HOLD a persistent per-reader model. Gloss-on-first-use maps cleanly BUT linear text has no zero-cost hover layer, so a gloss is never free — forces a real word-spend judgment.

consolidation.summary: Cycle 2 (3-agent prior-art sweep) consolidated & verified fresh. Convergent across independent searches. DOMINANT finding: expertise-reversal effect — for an expert wanting peer register the novice toolkit is actively HARMFUL (load + condescension); correct default is minimal/pointer register, depth added ONLY on a detected miss. This scientifically backs the user's 'don't talk down' and reshapes the tutor to default-quiet. Two-tier short-then-deep is the universal in-flow shape. Fading via contingency rule (register down on fluent use, up on stumble, read off the user's OWN writing) is how familiarity is OBSERVED not guessed/chore. ITS gives the skeleton: concept book = student model as an OVERLAY on the architecture map (domain model), tutor = tutoring model. Pocock's learning-records-as-ADRs is the most stealable state layer. The personalized-expert-reader-in-flow niche is UNFILLED — validates building new. THE GENUINELY-NOVEL CORE we'd invent: the calibration+interleaving problem — hold a standing per-reader familiarity model AND blend one paragraph of explanation into a working text stream without condescending or cluttering. No existing tool solves this (all assume a mismatched reader/medium).

reshapes.K5 concept book: best realized as a per-concept OVERLAY on the architecture map (student-over-domain), familiarity updated by contingent fading from the user's own writing; entries shaped like Pocock learning-records/ADRs (append-only, numbered, non-obvious-insight); freshness-stamped.
reshapes.K7 tutor: default NEAR-SILENT / minimal register; teaches only the delta, only on a detected miss or the user's pushback (matches T-A). Expert blind spot => still surface the genuinely-new delta.
reshapes.K9 milestone explainer: = Diataxis explanation quadrant, two-tier (terse default + deep on demand), freshness-stamped; interleaving into the stream is the unsolved part.
reshapes.register/tone (K3/T-G): expertise-reversal gives the rule: peer/minimal by default, add depth on miss; concept-local (expert on A, novice on new B).
